title: What Does the Bible Say About Slavery? 26 Verses
description: What the Bible says about slavery: the laws in Exodus and Leviticus, Paul and Philemon, the ban on kidnapping and the verses on freedom, in full.
keywords: what does the bible say about slavery
summary: The Bible regulates slavery in the Law of Moses (Exodus 21:2-11, Leviticus 25:39-46) and tells slaves and masters how to behave in the New Testament (Ephesians 6:5-9, Colossians 3:22-4:1) without commanding its end. It also condemns kidnapping people to sell them (Exodus 21:16, 1 Timothy 1:10), orders that an escaped slave not be returned (Deuteronomy 23:15-16), and says that in Christ there is no slave or free (Galatians 3:28). The World English Bible translates the Greek doulos as slave in 39 verses, while the King James Version has the word in only 2 and uses servant or bondman elsewhere, so the same passage can read very differently between the two. The verses below cover the laws, the apostles' instructions and the freedom passages.

faqs.a: The Bible assumes slavery existed and sets rules for it, including a six-year limit for Hebrew slaves (Exodus 21:2) and the death penalty for kidnapping (Exodus 21:16). It does not issue a general command to abolish it. Christians have read it both ways in history; abolitionists drew on Exodus, Philemon and Galatians 3:28, and those who defended slavery cited the regulating passages.

faqs.q: What does Philemon say about slavery?
faqs.a: Paul sends the runaway Onesimus back to Philemon and asks him to receive him 'no longer as a bondservant, but more than a bondservant, a beloved brother' (Philemon 1:16). Paul does not command release outright, but the letter treats a slave as an equal in Christ.

faqs.q: Why do translations say servant in one Bible and slave in another?
faqs.a: The Greek doulos means a person owned by another. The King James Version usually renders it servant or bondman (the word slave appears in 2 verses), while the World English Bible uses slave in 39. Several modern translations restore slave for the same reason.

faqs.q: What verses say the opposite of slavery?
faqs.a: Galatians 3:28 (no slave or free in Christ), Galatians 5:1 (Christ set us free), Luke 4:18 (liberty to the captives), Isaiah 58:6 (break every yoke) and 1 Timothy 1:9-10 (slave traders are among the lawless).
